title: Scalar Finite-Proper-Time Field Theory as Spectral Operator Calculus
abstract: We formulate a finite-proper-time construction for Euclidean scalar $λφ^4$ theory in which a retained endpoint $s_0$ is assigned to complete internal histories rather than independently to individual Schwinger segments. The theory is defined through paired open and closed spectral functions and their Fréchet/Duhamel hierarchy. Functional differentiation inserts operators along an existing proper-time history and partitions its total length, while interaction vertices sew separately complete histories. We introduce a corresponding complete-history diagrammatic calculus and derive the resulting one- and two-loop structures. We distinguish the retained endpoint from an auxiliary regulator or renormalisation-group scale and test whether its effects survive ordinary parameter matching and admissible field redefinitions. For the one-loop four-point function, fixing the renormalised mass, field normalisation, and quartic coupling leaves a finite momentum-dependent remainder. We establish a perturbative non-redundancy description of the retained endpoint against finite renormalisable-parameter redefinitions and local $S$-matrix-preserving field redefinitions at this order. The low-energy theory can be represented as an effective field theory, but its higher-derivative coefficients are not independent. This provides a concrete distinction between a retained finite proper-time scale and an arbitrary cutoff prescription.
summary: This work develops a Finite-Proper-Time Field Theory framework for $\lambda\phi^4$ theory, treating a finite endpoint scale $s_0$ as a physical parameter. By calculating loop corrections to scattering amplitudes, the authors prove that this retained scale introduces non-redundant physics that cannot be removed by standard renormalization procedures or local field redefinitions.
main_problem: To formulate a finite-proper-time construction for Euclidean scalar $\lambda\phi^4$ theory and rigorously determine if the dependence on the retained endpoint scale ($s_0$) survives standard renormalization procedures.
main_result: The analysis establishes that the retained finite proper-time scale $s_0$ introduces perturbative non-redundancy in scattering amplitudes, meaning it cannot be absorbed by local field redefinitions or parameter matching at one loop and beyond.
method: The authors use functional methods involving paired open/closed spectral functions and a complete-history diagrammatic calculus to calculate effective actions and scattering amplitudes up to two loops.
model_or_system: The theory analyzed is the Euclidean scalar $\lambda\phi^4$ model. The core novelty lies in defining the theory via a 'retained finite proper-time' scale ($s_0$), which differs fundamentally from standard UV cutoffs ($\Lambda_{UV}$) or renormalization group scales ($\mu$).
key_observables: The one-loop four-point scattering amplitude, specifically its on-shell dependence and the correlation between coefficients in the low-energy effective action.
important_parameters: The retained finite proper-time scale $s_0$, which is treated as a physical parameter distinct from regulators or renormalization scales.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to fixed-order Euclidean calculations, and the authors explicitly state that this does not imply nonperturbative Lorentzian completion or solve all open questions regarding field redefinition equivalence.

paper_structure: The paper builds by first introducing the FPT formalism using spectral functions and deriving diagrammatic rules. It then calculates loop corrections (one-loop four-point function) to demonstrate that $s_0$ dependence is non-redundant, culminating in theorems proving this non-equivalence to standard local renormalization schemes.
why_interesting: While the model is simple ($\lambda\phi^4$), the methodology of distinguishing between physical scales ($s_0$) and arbitrary regulators provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding how scale dependence enters quantum field theories beyond traditional RG flow descriptions.

figures.caption: Figure 1: The two two-loop one-particle-irreducible topologies generated by the background-field cumulant expansion: (a) the figure-eight from one quartic fluctuation vertex and (b) the sunset from two cubic fluctuation vertices.

Figure 2: Schematic of the Schwinger parameter worldlines which form the two-loop effective action. The left diagram refers to the first term in Eq. (94), and the right diagram refers to the second. Each line has minimum length s0. Each derivative acting on exponential factors in the Duhamel chain inserts an insertion which partitions a line (see Fig. 3), and subsequent derivatives acting on insertions modify their structure. They can be used to construct insertion-distribution diagrams, as explained in Section 15.2.

Figure 3: Duhamel ancestry of one complete open history. A functional derivative inserts an operator and partitions the same total proper time T into non-negative segments. Repeated differentiation produces further segments, but the only lower-endpoint condition is on their sum, P j uj = T ≥s0.

Figure 4: Dimensionless coincident finite-endpoint covariance in four dimensions, Rs0(x, x)/m2 = [e−z/z −E1(z)] /(16π2) with z = m2s0 = m2/Λ2. The quantity is finite for every fixed s0 > 0 and diverges as Rs0(x, x)/m2 ∼1/(16π2z) only in the limit s0 →0+ when the endpoint is removed.
Figure 5: Schematic one-loop one-particle-irreducible two-point kernel: the tree inverse kernel plus the scalar tadpole self-energy.
